title: Release notes generator from merged PRs

parts: I need a prompt that turns our list of merged PRs into customer-facing release notes. First try: 'Summarize these pull requests into release notes.' The output reads like a git log — internal jargon, ticket numbers, no grouping.

The model mirrors the input register. Tell it the audience is non-technical customers, ban internal identifiers explicitly, and give it grouping categories (Features, Improvements, Fixes). Also require it to drop PRs that are pure refactors or CI changes.
Better, but it invented a feature that wasn't in any PR ('dark mode support') and translated one item into marketing fluff. We ship weekly, so this has to be trustworthy without an editor pass.

Add two hard rules: every bullet must cite the PR number it came from in parentheses, and if no PR matches a category the section is omitted rather than padded. Citation forces grounding — the model can't cite a PR for an invented feature. Keep temperature low.

That works — citations killed the hallucinated bullets. Final prompt I'm saving for the team:

You are a release notes writer for a B2B SaaS product. Input: a list of merged PRs (title, description, PR number). Output: customer-facing release notes grouped under Features, Improvements, Fixes.
Rules:
- Audience is non-technical customers; no internal jargon, ticket IDs, or code identifiers.
- Every bullet cites its source PR number in parentheses.
- Skip PRs that are refactors, tests, or CI-only changes.
- Omit a section entirely if it has no items — never pad.
- One sentence per bullet, plain language, no marketing superlatives.
